Subject: Backup deletion propagation question — GreenBank EU instances

Hi Alex / Marissa,

Quick question from procurement/compliance as we review Redwood for our EU customer workloads: when a customer issues a deletion request for customer data (e.g., subject access / right to be forgotten), what is the observable timeline for that deletion to be reflected across backups and DR replicas? Specifically: 

- If a primary record is deleted (legal hold not active), how long until the tombstone/mark is written everywhere?
- When does a full expunge (permanent removal from offsite backups/replicas) typically complete for EU-only tenants?
- Do you provide evidence/artifacts (audit log entries or hashes) that a deletion propagated?

We have strict regulatory wording to satisfy; procurement asked for a short paragraph we can include in the SOW about backup expunge timelines and what evidence you can provide.

Thanks — Caroline

Thanks Caroline — good and important questions. High level answers up front, then I can loop in infra/ops for precise artifacts.

High-level:
- Tombstone/mark: when a delete is accepted the primary store marks the object immediately (milliseconds) and that tombstone is written to the change log and queued for replication.
- Replication visibility: most replicas will observe the tombstone within minutes under normal conditions; cross-region replication may take longer depending on in-flight writes and network windows.
- Expunge: permanent removal from backup snapshots / long-term archives depends on retention and our GC sweep. For EU-only tenants on a dedicated retention policy we typically surface expunge within 24–72 hours; worst-case (stalled replica + scheduled archive job) can be up to 7 days.
- Evidence: we can provide time-stamped audit log entries and a signed attestation that lists the deletion event and the snapshot waves that were purged. We can also provide object-hash removal proof for specific keys on request.

I'm attaching our current retention matrix (backup-retention-matrix-v2.xlsx) which maps snapshot windows to expunge waves. Will loop in Vivek for exact SLA language and any firm guarantees we can commit to in the SOW.

— Alex

Hi all — tagging in engineering/ops details and an authoritative timeline. I'll keep this concise and operational.

Flow & timelines (EU region-locked tenants, normal operating conditions):
- Delete acceptance: request processed by API -> primary store tombstone written (T0). This is synchronous from the API perspective; the event ID is returned immediately.
- Propagation to replicas: tombstone is appended to the replication log; typical visibility on active replicas is within minutes (T0 + 2–15 minutes).
- Snapshot / backup waves: we take incremental snapshots hourly and full checkpoint snapshots nightly (configurable per tenant). Snapshots that pre-date the deletion can include the object until the next snapshot wave is GC'd.
- GC / expunge window: our background GC marks eligible objects for physical removal during scheduled expunge waves. For EU tenants with the EU retention profile we operate a prioritized expunge queue: most deletes are physically removed from warm backups in 24–72 hours (T0 + 1–3 days).
- Long-tail cases: if a snapshot is archived to cold storage or a replica had significant lag, complete removal can take up to 7 days (T0 + up to 7 days). We treat legal holds and open support restores as exceptions — these are flagged in the audit trail and surface in the customer portal and to our support team.

On multi-tenant mounts / restore testing: we run restores into isolated, ephemeral environments that are tenant-scoped. We do not mount archived snapshots across tenants. Any restore used for DR testing is performed in a tenant-specific VPC or isolated namespace to prevent cross-tenant leakage. If a customer requests a shared lab test, we will sanitize snapshot contents per the customer's retention policy before any shared access.

Evidence and attestation:
- We can provide: time-stamped audit log entries for the delete API call (event ID, principal, timestamp), replication log entries confirming tombstone propagation (log sequence ids), and a signed attestation PDF that lists the snapshot waves removed and the timelines.
- Delivery timelines: audit logs and replication log excerpts we can produce within 3 business days; a formatted, signed attestation can be provided within 7 business days. If GreenBank requires the attestation inside 10 business days, we can meet that comfortably — exception handling (e.g., legal hold) would be called out explicitly.

Recommended SOW language (suggested single paragraph you can use):
"Redwood will, upon receipt of a valid deletion request for data subject to EU residency requirements, mark the object as deleted immediately and propagate the tombstone to replicas. Physical removal from warm backups and snapshots will be completed in 24–72 hours under normal operating conditions; in exceptional cases (archived snapshots or significant replica lag) removal may take up to 7 calendar days. Redwood will provide time-stamped audit log entries and a signed attestation documenting the deletion event and the snapshot waves removed within 10 business days of request."

If you want, I can produce a short one-page attestation template and a sample audit excerpt for your procurement team.

— Vivek
